task: Identify and characterise the ZolikaPatch [Options] keys that have no recovered patch signature in evidence/option_signatures.json.
generated_from: ZolikaPatch_extracted/ZolikaPatch.asi (read-only: section table, .rdata pattern strings, initial values, .reloc table)
method: A key belongs to the gap set iff it occurs in the INI [Options] section and is NOT a key of evidence/option_signatures.json.

Per key the loader dispatch arm is the byte range beginning at the push of the key string (minus the 5-byte push, i.e. at the preceding default-value push) and ending where the next key arm begins. CarDynamicShadowFix has no pushed key literal - its name is composed at run time - so its arm was delimited manually from the composed read at 0x1005458e.

Facts come from (a) the arm, (b) the option handler named in option_handlers.json, and (c) one level into its non-shared feature callees. A callee is a shared helper when >=3 distinct option arms reach it (key reader FUN_1005C160, key-string builder FUN_10058620, std::string helpers, strtol wrapper FUN_100014B0, VirtualProtect tail FUN_1005D630), so it is not attributable to one key.

Patterns are recovered three ways: the literal form FUN_10003830("...") / FUN_1005AFA0(&v,"..."); the register-held form, by walking back from every scanner call to the mov that loads ecx/edx and reading the .rdata string it points at; and the compiled-pattern form, where FUN_10058620 is fed a hex-byte string that FUN_100030a0 then compiles.
Module-relative writes are detected in two shapes: literal offsets (DAT_1015ad70 + 0xNNNN) and register-relative stores (mov reg,[0x1015AD70] ... mov [reg(+off)],value).
Every recovered pattern was run through the read-only game scanner; the hit count and the first hit addresses are recorded.

classification_definition.flag-only: sets a global flag and performs no patch action of its own
classification_definition.function-call-only: reaches a real patch action (signature scan, literal write, module-relative write or non-shared callee) but does not itself write a module-relative offset in the literal form
classification_definition.rva-patch: writes at one or more module-relative offsets from the module base (DAT_1015AD70)
classification_definition.unresolved: no patch action and no known flag could be attributed to the key

options_whose_ultimate_patch_target_is_u.note: These gap keys are classified function-call-only because an action WAS attributed to them, but the action delegates through an indirect call whose target lives in a zero-initialised plugin global. caveats: Nothing in the original package was modified; the ASI, the game executable and all existing evidence files were opened read-only. The reference ZIPs were never opened.
Game hit counts are direct byte searches over the immutable GTAIV.exe .text. A hit count > 1 means the original needed a per-build or per-site selection rule; that rule is not recovered here.
The CarPartsShadowFix pattern is DERIVED: it was re-assembled from the handler decimal digit loop and is not a literal in any artifact. It is marked assembled=true.
FreezeCarFix gate relationship to the DebugPrintSpawns block is read off the branch target (jne 0x10053FDB) and agrees with the INI note; the intent is inferred, not proven.

For every unresolved indirect slot the runtime target lives in a zero-initialised plugin global with no resolvable static writer and no relocation entry, so it cannot be recovered from the supplied artifacts.
evidence/option_flag_map.json still carries a stale entry for FixPCIDKickbug and FreezeCarFix (kind "call"/null); this file records the control-flow evidence rather than adopting that classification.
This file is derived evidence and is not wired into the Makefile, so `make test` and the existing evidence checkers are unaffected.

follow_up_recovery.note: Follow-up: LaunchWithPlayGTAIV and SuperLODFix were reported with 0 rows in the primary op table. SuperLODFix is now recovered as two module-RVA relative-jump installs (RVAs 0x4a3ce9/0x540e19 -> 0x100469e0) by tools/extract_rva_jumps.py, and LoadDLCs' own relative-jump installs are recovered too. LaunchWithPlayGTAIV writes two 4-byte immediates ('Play'/'V.ex') into a buffer reached by a runtime register, which is not a game-memory patch and is not modelled as an op row.
